LESSON: TRANSPORT

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: BIOLOGY
Strand: Anatomy and Physiology of Plants
Topic 2.2: Transport
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 18

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Transport, part of Anatomy and Physiology of Plants in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 BIOLOGY.

Key inquiry question: How are materials transported in plants?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Transport together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: The learner objectively analyses results of the bark ringing/girdling

experiment to demonstrate evidence of translocation.

● Imagination and Creativity: The learner seeks clarification from others while carrying out the experiment to

demonstrate the mechanisms of water and mineral salt uptake.

● Digital Literacy: A learner acquires technological competency through the use of digital devices with assistive devices

to search for information on uptake of water and mineral salts from the soil through the roots and translocation of food

substances from the leaves.

Values:
● Responsibility: The learner takes care of trees during the bark ringing/girdling experiment to observe translocation in

plants.

● Integrity: The learner displays honesty and truthfulness while reporting their findings on the mechanism of

translocation of manufactured food from the leaves.

29

● Social Justice: Learners work harmoniously during discussions of structures of external parts of a plant in relation to

functions.

Suggested Learning Materials

• Print and non-print materials, ink/dyes, transparent bags, realia, polythene bags, light bulbs, improvised fan

• Digital devices with assistive technology such as screen readers, talkback, refreshable braille display, screen

magnifiers

• Reference materials in print with appropriate font size and colour contrast

• Braille reference materials

Key Skills:

● Ability to relate structures of the plant transport system to their functions in plants,

● Demonstrate factors that affect the rate of transpiration in plants,
